milestones.diagramNote: Two ways to run steps: hosted in a sandbox, or on your own machines connected outward.
done: Organisations cannot see each other, proven by a test.
A step in a sandbox cannot reach anything but the internet.
Usage is metered and shown before it is billed.
Audit entries are chained and exportable.
The compliance pack lists each control with its evidence.

deepDives.title: The hosted service and sandboxed runners

groups.name: Hosted service and demo
groups.blurb: Use Launchway without running it, on a plan that follows your choices.

items.title: Hosted service
items.value: Launchway as a service: sign-up, quotas, usage metering, a free tier, pay for use, every option on every plan, and data residency.
items.detail: Price follows your choices, such as availability and users, and no feature is held back by plan.

items.title: Free tier and pay for use
items.value: A free tier, and pay-for-use billing from the start, with no extras for basics.
items.detail: Usage is metered and shown before it is billed.

items.title: Data residency
items.value: Choose where your data lives.
items.detail: Region choices are shown at sign-up and recorded.

items.title: Runners on your machines
items.value: Runners on your own servers or clusters connect out to the hosted engine, so code and secrets never leave your network.
items.detail: Only outbound connections are needed.

items.title: Sandboxed hosted runners
items.value: Each step in its own isolated machine, with no route to anything but the internet and firm quotas; the same profile available to any self-hosted server.
items.detail: Layers of isolation back each other up, and a kill switch exists at the network.

items.title: Hosted capacity that can grow
items.value: Everything is portable, so capacity can be added on any provider as demand justifies.
items.detail: Nothing is tied to one machine.

items.title: A public demo
items.value: A safe instance on the internet with realistic data anyone can explore, read-only at first. A local demo already runs from the quick start.
items.detail: Try it with your own runner follows once organisation isolation exists.

items.title: Organisations
items.value: Several organisations on one installation, isolated from each other, with the level names you choose.
items.detail: Isolation is tested.

groups.name: Identity, audit and compliance
groups.blurb: The controls enterprises and regulated teams ask for.

items.title: Built-in accounts with MFA
items.value: Small teams without an identity provider still get secure sign-in with authenticator codes or passkeys.
items.detail: Recovery codes and session management are included.

items.title: Directory groups and custom roles
items.value: LDAP and Active Directory groups mapped to roles at each level, leavers removed automatically, and a view of who can do what, and why.
items.detail: Roles are custom and permissions are clear.

items.title: Other single sign-on and provisioning
items.value: SAML sign-in and automatic user provisioning for larger companies.
items.detail: Works beside directory groups.

items.title: Tamper-evident audit and SIEM export
items.value: An audit trail nobody can quietly edit, streamed to your security tools.
items.detail: Entries are chained so a gap shows.

items.title: Retention, legal hold and encryption at rest
items.value: Choose how long data is kept, prove deletion, and encrypt logs and artifacts with rotating keys; encrypted by default when hosted.
items.detail: A hold overrides cleanup.

items.title: A compliance pack for PCI DSS and HIPAA
items.value: Policy templates and an evidence report that maps controls to requirements. It supports your compliance work and is not a certification.
items.detail: Controls are listed with evidence.

items.title: Zero trust throughout
items.value: Every service, runner and person proves identity on every call.
items.detail: No shared secrets between components.

milestones.name: Beyond delivery
milestones.promise: Ideas that grow naturally from one connected platform. Planned, but behind everything above.
milestones.audience: Teams that, once delivery is in one place, want to operate what they ship from the same place.
milestones.what: These are ideas that grow from one connected platform. They are planned, but they come after everything above.
scenarios: You see what each service costs next to what it delivers.
A pipeline step breaks a pre-production environment on purpose and checks that verification notices.
A new engineer finds a service, its owner, its docs and its last deployment in one directory.

groups.name: Operate what you ship
groups.blurb: Ideas that grow naturally from one connected platform.

items.title: Cloud cost management
items.value: See what each service, team and environment costs to run, next to what it delivers.
items.detail: Includes the cost of runner pools.

items.title: Chaos testing
items.value: Deliberately break things in a pre-production environment as a pipeline step, and see whether verification notices.
items.detail: Built-in host experiments and well-known chaos tools are supported.

items.title: A developer portal and service catalogue
items.value: A directory of every service with its owner, health, docs and deployments.
items.detail: Built on the same data as everything else.

items.title: Smaller integrations
items.value: Chat approvals, feature-flag mitigation and more event sources.
items.detail: Added by demand.

items.title: Discussions and snippets
items.value: A forum for projects and shareable snippets.
items.detail: Optional and off by default.

items.title: Cloud development environments
items.value: Ready-made environments to work on a project from a browser.
items.detail: Reuses preview environments.

items.title: Runtime and API protection
items.value: Protect running services from known attack patterns.
items.detail: Builds on traffic protection.

items.title: Ticket to code agent
items.value: An agent that takes a work item to a proposed change.
items.detail: A person always reviews.

items.title: Attestation programme
items.value: Publish signed attestations about how Launchway itself is built.
items.detail: Everyone can verify.

principles.title: Everything, without the mess
principles.value: Every feature uses the same objects, permissions, audit trail and policy point, and nothing switched off appears in the menus.

principles.title: One way in, every way in
principles.value: A wizard for each task, with the same operation in the HTTP API, the agent endpoint, the command line and Terraform.

principles.title: Only a database and Git
principles.value: Everything else is built in; outside integrations stay optional.

principles.title: Boring upgrades
principles.value: One binary and a database, additive migrations, an older binary running on a newer schema, and rollback by image.

principles.title: High availability and security are part of done
principles.value: A feature says what happens when a server, the database or a runner dies, and who may do what, before it merges.

principles.title: Honest status
principles.value: An item is available only when it is merged, tested and documented. Order is by value and is not a schedule.
